title: A smooth algebra over an arbitrary reduced ring is reduced
statement: Let $R$ and $A$ be commutative rings and let $\varphi:R\to A$ be a smooth ring map [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. If $R$ is reduced, meaning that $r^n=0$ for $r\in R$ and $n\geq1$ implies $r=0$, then $A$ is reduced in the same sense. No Noetherian hypothesis or finiteness assumption beyond smoothness is imposed.

source.place: Tag 033B (lemma-reduced-goes-up), full statement, including the non-Noetherian case.

proof.text: First let $T\to B$ be any smooth map with $T$ Noetherian. Smoothness includes finite presentation by [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], hence finite type, so $B$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. The map is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-flat]. For every prime $\mathfrak p$ of $T$ and every finite purely inseparable extension $k\prime/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition] makes $k\prime\otimes_TB$ smooth over $k\prime$. This ring is Noetherian by the same finite-type theorem (a field has only the ideals zero and the whole field), and every prime localization is regular local by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-field-regular-local]. Thus it is regular by [def-weil-regular-scheme]. The fibre after extension from $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ to $k\prime$ is this ring: [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change] gives $k\prime\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}(\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_TB)\cong k\prime\otimes_TB$. Consequently each fibre is geometrically regular, and the map $T\to B$ is regular by [def-weil-pbc-g-ring].

source.place: Tag 033B, lemma-reduced-goes-up, first paragraph; Tags 00T4, 00TT, 00FN; geometric regularity defined in Tag 0382 and More on Algebra Tag 07BZ

proof.text: If in addition $T$ is reduced, the preceding step supplies both Noetherian hypotheses and regularity required by [lem-exc-regular-map-reduced-target]. Apply that statement to conclude that $B$ is reduced. This proves the Noetherian case needed below without imposing any Noetherian hypothesis on the original $R$.

source.place: Tag 033B, lemma-reduced-goes-up, first paragraph; the regular-map variant is More on Algebra Tag 07QK, lemma-reduced-goes-up

proof.text: For the given $R\to A$, use [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-algebra-finite-type-model] to choose a finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-subalgebra $R_0\subseteq R$, a smooth $R_0\to A_0$, and an $R$-algebra isomorphism $A\cong R\otimes_{R_0}A_0$. Let $P$ be the collection of finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-subalgebras $T\subseteq R$ containing $R_0$. It contains $R_0$; adjoining the two finite generating sets gives an upper bound for two members, and adjoining any $r\in R$ to the generators of $R_0$ gives a member containing $r$. Thus $P$ is nonempty, directed and covers $R$ elementwise.

source.place: Tag 033B, lemma-reduced-goes-up, second paragraph, descent to a finite-type subring; Tag 00TP, lemma-finite-presentation-fs-Noetherian

proof.text: For each $T\in P$, put $B_T=T\otimes_{R_0}A_0$. The map $T\to B_T$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition]. The ring $T$ is reduced: if $t^n=0$ in $T$, its image in $R$ is zero by reducedness of $R$, hence $t=0$ because $T\subseteq R$ is injective. The ring $\mathbf Z$ is Noetherian since every ideal is generated by its least positive element, or is zero. As $T$ is finite type over $\mathbf Z$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] makes it Noetherian. Steps 1 and 2 now show that every $B_T$ is reduced.

source.place: Tag 033B, lemma-reduced-goes-up, second paragraph, enlarging the finite-type subring and applying the Noetherian case

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-directed-subalgebra-tensor-colimit] to $P$, $R_0$ and $A_0$. It gives a small filtered ring diagram whose stages are ring-isomorphic to the $B_T$ and whose colimit is ring-isomorphic to $R\otimes_{R_0}A_0$, hence to $A$. Every stage is reduced by step 4. Given $x\in A$ with $x^n=0$, $n\geq1$, transfer $x$ to this colimit. Clause (1) of [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise] represents it by $y$ in a stage $i$. Its power $y^n$ and $0$ have equal images. Clause (2) gives a stage $j$ and arrows from $i$ to $j$ with the image of $y^n$ along the first equal to the image of $0$ along the second. Thus the image of $y$ along the first arrow has nth power zero in the reduced ring at $j$, and is zero. Cocone compatibility gives $x=0$. The two arrows need not coincide, since every ring map sends zero to zero. This proves reducedness for all positive exponents and completes the arbitrary-base case.

source.place: Tag 033B, lemma-reduced-goes-up, second paragraph, lifting the element and its relation to a later stage; the same argument works with any positive exponent
